title: Near-identical yearly counts are new people, not copies
question: Where an activity's yearly count barely moves, are the records carried forward from the year before?
finding: Near-identical yearly counts show no sign of records carried forward. 8 activity year-pairs differ by 1% or less; in none is the mix of age, income, race group and neighbourhood the same (80% at most overlaps), and client numbers rarely recur. Moving-cost and deposit help, for example, has 338 and 340 records in 2015-16 and 2016-17 with 36% of the mix in common.
how: For each activity and consecutive pair of fiscal years with at least 10 records each and counts within 1%: the share of records whose race x income x age x neighbourhood cell is matched in the other year, and the client numbers in both years.
limits: A fixed count can come from a fixed number of slots or a fixed budget per award; overlap of cells is a coarse test and cannot see individual people.
